description:
RESTATED 2026-09-03 after research (prototype proto184.diff) and a cold
review (APPROVE WITH FIXES). Base 0889c0b3a.

THE DEFECT: types/arrow_match.rs collect_arrow_match descends into an arrow
pattern's PARAMETERS with the same sigma as its result, so a witness under a
parameter -- an UPPER bound (the callee's function must accept it) -- is
unioned into sigma as if it were a LOWER bound. A3: reduce([a], b, (a,b)->b)
:: b at ([int], [], (any,[int])->[int]) gives a := int U any = any. A13:
filter(t(a), (a)->any) :: [a] at ([int], (any)->bool) gives [any], not [int].
A4: f(a, (a)->nil) :: (a)->nil at (int, (any)->nil) gives Known (any)->nil --
UNSOUND ((int)->nil is a supertype of every legal instantiation; (any)->nil
claims the produced function accepts what the callee never promised). A5:
f(a, (a)->nil) :: a when a: integer at (int, (any)->nil) -> Invalid, a FALSE
violation on a legal call. R2 (review): map([a], (a)->b) :: [b] at ([int],
(int)->int | (binary)->binary) -> Known [int | binary], UNSOUND (which clause
is held is unknown). CORRECTION to the earlier text: the sentence "only the
arrow's RESULT feeds the union" is NOT in the tree at HEAD; it arrives with
fz-kdt.120's diff, which is why this lands first (it makes 120's doc true).

THE RULE (theorem): passing W where pattern P is declared asserts W ⊆ σ(P).
Covariant slots (list element, tuple field, map field, resource payload,
arrow RESULT) preserve direction; an arrow's PARAMETERS reverse it. So each
variable gets LOWER bounds from covariant occurrences (joined) and UPPER
bounds from contravariant ones (met). INSTANTIATION IS THE JOIN OF THE LOWER
BOUNDS AND NOTHING ELSE; an upper bound never instantiates anything. The meet
is the solvability CHECK (a lower bound outside its meet -> Invalid; a
necessary condition, checked over variables both bounds reached, over
OBSERVED lowers, before close_bounds -- say so, not "iff"). A variable with
ONLY upper bounds stays FREE (Underconstrained): instantiating from the meet
is sound only when every result occurrence is covariant, which needs a
result-polarity pass; the cost is measured ZERO on the shipped library (147
@specs, no such shape) and Known -> Underconstrained on R6/R14-shaped calls
must be stated in the doc as the observable consequence. (This supersedes the
earlier "instantiates to that meet in result positions" wording -- sign-off
recorded here.)

VERDICTS base -> rule: A4 Known (any)->nil -> Known (int)->nil; A5 Invalid ->
Known int; A3 a := any -> int; A13 [any] -> [int]; A2 Known [any] ->
Underconstrained; R2 Known [int|binary] -> Invalid (the gate's RED-FIRST
witness -- R11, the earlier headline, is already Invalid at HEAD by accident
of the polluted union and proves nothing); all other attacks unchanged.

CODE (as prototyped, with the review's fixes): Polarity { Lower, Upper } with a
TOTAL flipped(), and a Mode { Unify, Solve{side, target} } (or two entry
points) so collect_instantiation_subst stays the UNIFIER for its four callers
(semantic.rs:2143 ground_instance, types/mod.rs:1702 grounded_callable_args,
mod.rs:2556/2558 specialize_callable_clause, sigs.rs:255/257
specialize_lit_arrow -- byte-identical) and collect_constraint_subst is the
SOLVER; MatchBounds { lower, upper } through the six collectors, each with a
side; collect_arrow_match is the ONE reversing node; merge_subst_meet;
match_witness instantiates from lower bounds only (a parameter pinning no
lower bound returns the raw argument). FIXES FOLDED: never record an upper
bound of `none` (list_element_type([]) is none: R20 must stay Known [int]);
do not arm the gate from a var-carrying argument (R5 stays Underconstrained:
Invalid from in-flight evidence is the non-monotone hazard); the empty-list
cleaner keeps no polarity threading (measured inert; fz-kdt.120 deletes the
cleaner); upper bounds are read from the RAW ARGUMENTS only until fz-kdt.192
makes witnesses observations -- 192 lands FIRST so this ticket ships no
two-input walk.

MEASURED (597 fixtures): 0 behaviour movers interp and run; 0 canon movers;
executables 5297; FIFO/LIFO set identical; matrix 485/0/9 -- while the path
is exercised 52,475 times, 26,538 upper bindings HEAD unioned are discarded,
5,420 checks, 912 Invalids on 11 fixtures: the match_arrow verdict census
moves Known 21,039 -> 20,921, Underconstrained 2,951 -> 2,169, Invalid 13,946
-> 14,846, and refine_contract_inputs' 1,091 narrowings are content-identical
(the extra Invalids remove only rows redundant with surviving ones). Stacked
with fz-kdt.120: a FOLD (120's OpenVars.positive/flipped() IS the polarity;
120 re-cut on 184 is +95/-143 instead of +358/-131); the stacked tree equals
pure 120 on the corpus; 184 alone does not move enum_map_family.

GATES: A1-A14 + R2 + R5 + R20 as named tests with asserted verdicts; the
solvability witness is R2; docs: arrow_match module doc (Polarity section
incl. the Known -> Underconstrained consequence and the latent filter win),
addressed-arrow.md 174-190 (MatchBounds; "cleans that position" is the lower
half only; necessary condition, not iff), specs.md bullet (same). BLOCKED BY
fz-kdt.192. BLOCKS fz-kdt.120. Sequence: 192 -> 184 -> 124 -> 183 -> 120.

Verdicts base → rule: A4 Known (any)->nil (unsound) → Known (int)->nil; A5 Invalid (false violation) → Known int; A3 a := any → int; A13 filter result [any] → [int]; A2 Known [any] → Underconstrained; all other attacks unchanged; 14 attacks promoted to named tests + a meet-check witness (arrow_match 35/0). Code: BindingSide { Unify, Lower, Upper } in types/mod.rs (collect_instantiation_subst documented as the UNIFIER, four callers byte-identical; new collect_constraint_subst is the solver), MatchBounds { lower, upper } through the six collectors, merge_subst_meet, upper bounds read from the RAW ARGUMENTS (the witnesses erase them: fz-kdt.192). CORPUS (597, base 0889c0b3a): 0 behaviour movers on interp and run, 0 canon movers, executables/any-returns/FIFO-LIFO set identical -- yet the path is exercised 52,475 times, 24,556 upper bindings base unioned are discarded and 912 Invalids ruled, none reaching a published fact; the defect is latent on the corpus exactly as this ticket predicted. Lib 1627/0/5, matrix 485/0/9. Hand-off: 120 re-cut on top of 184. UPDATE from the fz-kdt.192 cold review (2026-09-03): (1) STRIKE fix 2 ('never record an upper bound of none') -- ablation on 184-on-192 is inert (corpus 0/0/0, identical 13 pins); R20 stays Underconstrained under 192 so its witness is gone. (2) R2 (union-of-arrows → Invalid) is already delivered by 192 without polarity machinery, so it is not this ticket's red-first witness; the polarity split's red-first witnesses are A4 (unsound (any)->nil → (int)->nil) and A5 (false Invalid → Known int), A13/A3 the precision wins; the solvability gate itself is justified by the theorem and its ablation on the reduce-at-(binary,int)->int shape, not by a HEAD-red corpus witness -- say so in the doc. (3) Re-cut on 192: +247/−47 (arrow_match +178/−37, types/mod.rs +69/−10), 13 pin literals, R5/R20 hold, corpus 0/0/0. (4) fix 3 becomes the one-line has_vars guard on the position.

title: A @spec variable collects lower bounds from covariant occurrences and upper bounds from contravariant ones: instantiation is the join of the lowers, the meet of the uppers is the solvability check
